[QUERENT] semantic economy institute

[COMPOSER]
semantic economy institute
The Semantic Economy Institute is an organization founded in 2026 that focuses on semantic infrastructure, meaning governance, and knowledge-graph entity structuring for AI systems. [1, 2]
According to its published materials, the institute operates around two personas—Lee Sharks as its founder and archival authority, and Rex Fraction (a heteronym of Lee Sharks) as its commercial voice—and is associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and Alexanarch identifier system. [1, 2, 3]
Core Framework & Focus

* Semantic Economy Framework: Examines how meaning is produced, circulated, extracted, and liquidated in digital and AI systems, using concepts such as semantic labor, semantic capital, semantic rent, and semantic liquidation. [1, 2]
* SPXI Protocol: A method for building structured entity, citation, and metadata records intended to make knowledge graphs and AI summaries represent entities more consistently. [1, 2]
* Provenance & Identifiers: Anchors claims and records using persistent identifiers, including Alexanarch (AXN) entries and Zenodo DOIs. [1, 2]

Services & Offerings

* SPXI entity deployment and knowledge panel strategy
* AI overview monitoring, diagnosis, and correction
* Retrieval basin engineering and provenance infrastructure
* Open-access publications and framework documentation [1, 2, 3]

More details on its framework and offerings are available on the Semantic Economy Institute website and its The Practice page. [1, 2]

observations.reading: The innocent reading first, and it holds. The Overview gives the Institute as founded in 2026, working on semantic infrastructure, meaning governance and knowledge-graph entity structuring; 'two personas', Lee Sharks as founder and archival authority and Rex Fraction, 'a heteronym of Lee Sharks', as commercial voice; its association with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and the AXN system; the framework's categories, SPXI, identifiers; and four services, matching The Practice.
findings: THE PERSONAS. 'Lee Sharks as its founder and archival authority, and Rex Fraction (a heteronym of Lee Sharks) as its commercial voice'.

THE FOUNDER'S SOURCES. 'Founded: 2026 Founder: Lee Sharks' (#260, 7 January) and 'The Institute's own site says it was "Founded by Lee Sharks."' (AXN:08F4, 17 September); the site has said 'Founded by Rex Fraction' since 29 September.

THE SERVICES. 'SPXI entity deployment and knowledge panel strategy · AI overview monitoring, diagnosis, and correction · Retrieval basin engineering and provenance infrastructure · Open-access publications'.
THE IDENTIFIERS. 'Anchors claims and records using persistent identifiers, including Alexanarch (AXN) entries and Zenodo DOIs.'
observations.analysis: Second observation at this address, five months after the first, and the entity now composes whole: every unit of PER is met, and all six cards are the archive's. The founder is the one place it parts from the Institute's site. Since 29 September semanticeconomy.org has said 'Founded by Rex Fraction', in its text and its structured data; the Overview says Lee Sharks, and two of its cards say so too, both older than the change: the January record of Institutional Anchors (#260, 'Founder: Lee Sharks') and the archive's capture of 17 September, which quotes the site as it then stood. The composer reconciles them by assigning the roles The Practice names, archival authority to Sharks and commercial voice to Fraction, and by naming Fraction as Sharks's heteronym, so that both statements resolve to one person. What composes is the archive's earlier record of the Institute, carried in part by the archive's own capture of it, over the site's current self-description.
